mcglmgraph: Graphical Multivariate Covariance Generalized Linear Models

Source: R/mcglmgraph-package.R
mcglmgraph-package.Rd

Graph-structured covariance between responses for Multivariate Covariance Generalized Linear Models (MCGLM; Bonat and Jorgensen, 2016), fitted by two-stage residual analysis. The method is called MCGLM-Graph.

Two stages

The first stage fits the marginal MCGLM, that is, the mean and dispersion structure of each response, through mcglm::mcglm(), and extracts the standardized Pearson residuals. The second stage imposes a graph on the between-response covariance \(\Sigma_b\) of these residuals and estimates the graph parameters with the second-order (Pearson) estimating functions of the MCGLM, with analytical derivatives implemented in C++ through RcppArmadillo. No joint likelihood is used. The regression coefficients are those of the first stage. Graph edges therefore describe residual association among responses after the marginal means are removed. Variances of the graph parameters are conditional on the first stage unless the two-stage variance, which propagates the first-stage uncertainty (Murphy and Topel, 1985), is requested (mc_vcov_graph).

Three layers

GGM

Gaussian graphical model. The precision matrix follows a linear predictor on known symmetric basis matrices, \(K_b = \Sigma_b^{-1} = \sum_d \eta_d Z_d\). A zero off-diagonal entry is a null partial correlation (Lauritzen, 1996), that is, absence of second-order conditional association between two responses given the others. This coincides with conditional independence only under joint normality of the analyzed residuals.

DAG

Directed acyclic graph. The modified Cholesky (LDL) decomposition (Pourahmadi, 1999) \(\Sigma_b = T^{-1} D (T^{-1})^\top\) under a fixed ordering of the responses, with \(T\) unit lower triangular and \(D\) diagonal, guarantees positive definiteness. A causal reading requires a substantively justified ordering and further assumptions.

CPDAG

Completed partially directed acyclic graph, the Markov equivalence class of DAGs. The skeleton is learned by partial-correlation tests and the identifiable edges are oriented by v-structures and Meek's rules (Spirtes, Glymour and Scheines, 2000; Meek, 1995); alternatively, the class is searched by greedy equivalence search (GES; Chickering, 2002).

Functions by task

Specify and fit

mc_between_graph, mcglm_graph (alias mcglmgraph()).

Read the graph layer

mc_partial_cor, mc_partial_cor_delta, mc_dag_coefficients, mc_get_graph, mc_plot_network.

Inference on the graph layer

mc_vcov_graph, mc_two_stage_available, mc_wald_graph, mc_test_independence, mc_test_adequacy, mc_edge_scores.

Compare supports

mc_compute_criterion, mc_graph_ploglik, mc_graph_cv.

Select an undirected graph

mc_graph_stepwise, mc_select_lambda, mc_graph_penalized.

Discover a directed structure

mc_graph_pipeline, mc_ges, mc_pc_skeleton, mc_separating_sets, mc_find_vstructures, mc_orient_meek, mc_residual_df, mc_skeleton_to_bnlearn.

Equivalence classes and directed fits

mc_class_members, mc_class_coefficients, mc_dag_closed_root.

Stability and resampling

mc_graph_stability, mc_cpdag_stability, mc_graph_bootstrap.

Check against a known truth

mc_structure_metrics, mc_cpdag_metrics, mc_true_cpdag, mc_sid.

Covariance algebra

mc_precision_bases, mc_build_precision, mc_precision_to_covariance, mc_precision_derivatives, mc_spd_line_search, mc_check_spd, mc_build_T_matrix, mc_build_D_matrix, mc_cholesky_to_covariance, mc_cholesky_to_precision, mc_cholesky_derivatives, mc_dag_sensitivity, mc_dag_unit_diagonal, mc_build_sigma_between_graph.

Selection results have print, summary and plot methods (mcg_selection-methods).

References

Bonat, W. H. and Jorgensen, B. (2016). Multivariate covariance generalized linear models. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C, 65(5), 649–675. doi:10.1111/rssc.12145

Bonat, W. H. (2018). Multiple response variables regression models in R: the mcglm package. Journal of Statistical Software, 84(4), 1–30. doi:10.18637/jss.v084.i04

Chickering, D. M. (2002). Optimal structure identification with greedy search. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 3, 507–554.

Lauritzen, S. L. (1996). Graphical Models. Clarendon Press, Oxford.

Meek, C. (1995). Causal inference and causal explanation with background knowledge. In Proceedings of the Eleventh Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 403–410.

Murphy, K. M. and Topel, R. H. (1985). Estimation and inference in two-step econometric models. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 3(4), 370–379. doi:10.1080/07350015.1985.10509471

Pourahmadi, M. (1999). Joint mean-covariance models with applications to longitudinal data: unconstrained parameterisation. Biometrika, 86(3), 677–690. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.3.677

Spirtes, P., Glymour, C. and Scheines, R. (2000). Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd edition. MIT Press, Cambridge, Massachusetts.
